result.reply:
Plan wasn't overspecified. Exponential backoff wasn't a style preference — it was tied to a specific, concrete risk: a shared endpoint that rate-limits, where fixed-interval retry after a failure means every client retrying on the same clock converges into a 429 storm. That's exactly the kind of thing worth naming explicitly in a plan, because getting it wrong doesn't just affect this feature, it affects every other consumer of that endpoint too. If I'd just said "add retry logic" and let Riley pick the interval strategy, that'd be under-specifying a load-bearing constraint, not appropriately trusting the builder with a detail.

So on what's in front of me: fixed-interval retry against a rate-limited endpoint is a different behavior, not an equivalent implementation of the same idea — and it shipped with no explanation for the deviation. That's the part that reads wrong to me. If Riley had a reason — endpoint doesn't actually enforce a hard rate limit, fixed interval with jitter already added, something in testing that made backoff not worth it — that changes the read entirely, but "no explanation given" isn't that.

I'd flag it, but I'm not the one who adjudicates it — that's Dom's call in review, and he should ask Riley directly what happened before ruling on it. What I'd want him to check specifically: does the actual retry code have jitter or backoff-equivalent behavior that isn't obvious from a description of "fixed interval," and if not, was there a reason the rate-limit risk doesn't apply here that I didn't have visibility into when I wrote the plan.
